title: Minimum Effort Control Using Variational Methods of Analytical Mechanics A New Approach For Optimal Control
summary: Modern optimal control theory involves adjoining the already known equations of motion of a dynamic system to the objective function using dynamic costates; this is done in order to constrain the optimal control solutions to satisfy the equations of motion. The use of costates increases the number of variables and hence increases the complexity of the problem. On the other hand, variational methods of analytical mechanics finds the equations of motion by minimizing an action functional of the dynamic system, realizing control forces as external input to the system.
